titles.463: Annotatio III §.X (3)(a): Praxis Christiana — first table; latria of what every sense calls bread and wine
titles.464: Annotatio III §.X (3)(a) cont.: Highest idolatry species — even without their Transsubstantiation hypothesis; God’s definition, not ours
titles.465: Annotatio III §.X (3)(b): Instituted praxis — cup as well as bread; Mass/Transsubstantiation snatches the cup from the laity

latin.463: (3.) Praxi Christiana, quà priorem Legis Divinæ Tabulam, (a) Naturali de toto Triuno Deo religiosâ veneratione colendo: quandoquidem in Missa illud ipsum, quod sensus omnes testantur panem ac vinum esse (speciebus seu accidentibus horum, non tantùm substantias suas oculis exponentibus, sed, ceu particulas, eorum constitutionem ingredientibus) summus Deus & creditur, & prædicatur esse, & illo ipso cultu, qui summo Deo proprius est, quique à pontificiis ipsis, per λατρείας nomen ab omni alio inferiori cultu discriminatur, Communicaturis, quin Missæ Celebrationi adstantibus quibusvis, adorandum præbetur atque edicitur.
latin.464: Hôcque ipso summa Idololatriæ species incurritur, ne Pontificiis quidem ipsis, sub hypothesi haud facta Transsubstantiationis, negata unquam, sed nec neganda citra hanc hypothesin, tùm quod hypotheseos suæ nullo vel Revelationis vel Rationis argumento, certiores fieri possint, multis è contrario utriusque argumentis, saltem dubii de ista reddantur, si non omnino ab eadem abducantur; tùm, quod Idololatriæ natura ac admissio, neutiquam ab hypothesi opinioneque humana, sive vera ista sit, sive falsa, sed verò à determinatione seu definitione Dei, dependeat, quâ toties idololatriam propriè sic dictam committi novimus, quoties id, quod summe Deus non est, sive ex errore, sive citra errorem, vel æstimatur, vel salutatur talis, nedum religioso summôque cultu afficitur.
latin.465: (b) Praxi Institutæ, quatenus hæc à Christo immediatè originem trahit, quâque non minùs ad Calicis vinique, quam panis usum, singulos Communicantes obstringit, per Missam interim & Transsubstantiationis rationem, Laicis cunctis eripiendum. Hoc pacto Transsubstantiatio etiam in posteriorem Divinæ Legis Tabulam impingit, Proximo id subducens, quod illi tribuendum expresso Christus mandato voluit per τὸ: Hoc facite, S. Coenam administraturis id omne designandum injungens, quod ipse administrans designaverat.
latin.466: (4.) Tàm Fidei, quam huic superstructæ praxi, primorum, per multa secula Christianorum: Quodsi enim primævi Christiani Transsubstantiationem professi fuissent, nemine eorum tùm temporis, veri sensus Christi verborum: Hoc est corpus meum, hic est sanguis meus, ignaro existente, quî fieri unquam potuisset, quò minùs ab his, præfervidis alioquin Mysteriarum Religionis suæ propugnatoribus, fama dogmatis, ad eos, quos inter vivebant, Judæos pariter atque Ethnicos, quam velocissimè transiisset citra omnem moram, non contradictiones horum ferias duntaxat, sed & exsibilationes quascunque expertura?
latin.467: Id quod tamen, vel semel, vel ab ullo hostium Christianæ sectæ infestissimorum, factitatum esse, nullibi, nec in ipsorum (Tryphonis puta, Celsi, Juliani, Porphyrii, omnem profectò ansam Dogmata Christiana calumniosissimè traducendi, quàm studiosè captantium) nec in cujuspiam ex diligentissimis Christianarum veritatum Assertoribus (quales Justinus Martyr, Tertullianus, Origenes, Arnobius & Minutius Felix memorantur) Scriptis Apologeticis expositum legimus.
latin.468: Thyesteas Coenas, quarum quandoque Christiani arguebantur, ad Gnosticos solos (non nisi per apertissimam malitiam Christianis annumeratos) pertinuisse, à veris autem Christianis, citra omnem Eucharistiæ S. mentionem injectam, nedum Mysterii hujus expositionem defensionemque susceptam vel minimam, pro mera calumnia habitas explosasque fuisse, notius est, quàm ut hoc loco prolixius dici debeat. Quin Praxios Rituumque, Transsubstantiationi indissolubiliter annexorum (quales sunt Sacramenti Adoratio, Elevatio, Circumgestatio) recentioribus seculis adinventæ, apud veteres Christianos constans atque perpetuus defectus, de Transsubstantiatione ab his penitus ignorata prolixè satis testari censendus est.

pass_a.463: (3.) By Christian Praxis, as to the prior Table of the Divine Law, (a) by religiously venerating the whole Triune God: since in the Mass that very thing which all the senses testify to be bread and wine (the species or accidents of these not only exposing their substances to the eyes, but entering as particles into their constitution) is both believed and preached to be the highest God, and is offered and commanded to be adored by communicants, nay by any standing at the Mass celebration, with that very cult proper to the highest God, which the Pontificians themselves discriminate by the name λατρεία from every other inferior cult.
pass_a.464: And by this itself the highest species of Idolatry is incurred — never denied even by the Pontificians themselves under a hypothesis of Transsubstantiation not made, and not to be denied apart from this hypothesis: both because they cannot be made more certain of their hypothesis by any argument of Revelation or of Reason, and by many arguments of either are at least rendered doubtful of it if not wholly led away from it; and because the nature and admission of Idolatry depends by no means on a human hypothesis and opinion, whether that be true or false, but truly on God’s determination or definition, by which we know idolatry properly so called is committed as often as that which is not the highest God, whether from error or without error, is either estimated or saluted as such, not to say affected with the highest religious cult.
pass_a.465: (b) By Instituted Praxis, insofar as this draws origin immediately from Christ, and by which it binds each Communicant no less to the use of the Cup and wine than of bread — to be snatched meanwhile from all the Laity by the Mass and the rationale of Transsubstantiation. By this pact Transsubstantiation also strikes against the posterior Table of the Divine Law, withdrawing from the Neighbor what Christ by express mandate willed given him through the τὸ: Do this, enjoining on those administering the Sacred Supper that they designate all that He Himself had designated while administering.
pass_a.466: (4.) Both to the Faith, and to the praxis built upon it, of the first Christians through many centuries: For if the earliest Christians had professed Transsubstantiation, none of them then being ignorant of the true sense of Christ’s words This is my body, this is my blood, how could it ever have been that the rumor of the dogma would not most swiftly, without any delay, have passed from these otherwise fervent defenders of their Religion’s Mysteries to the Jews and Gentiles among whom they lived — about to meet not only their serious contradictions but every kind of hissing?
pass_a.467: Yet that this was done even once, or by any of the most hostile enemies of the Christian sect, we read nowhere exposed — neither in their writings (say of Trypho, Celsus, Julian, Porphyry, who as studiously as possible seized every handle for most calumniously traducing Christian Dogmas) nor in the Apologetic writings of any of the most diligent Assertors of Christian truths (such as Justin Martyr, Tertullian, Origen, Arnobius and Minucius Felix are remembered).
pass_a.468: That the Thyestean Banquets of which Christians were sometimes accused pertained to the Gnostics alone (numbered with Christians only by most open malice), but by true Christians — without any mention of the Sacred Eucharist injected, much less the least exposition or defense of this Mystery undertaken — were held and exploded as mere calumny, is better known than need be said more lengthily here. Nay the constant and perpetual defect among the ancient Christians of the Praxis and Rites indissolubly annexed to Transsubstantiation (such as Adoration, Elevation, Circumgestation of the Sacrament), invented in more recent centuries, is to be judged to testify amply enough that Transsubstantiation was utterly unknown to them.

463: (3)(a) Christian praxis vs the first table: religious worship of the Triune God.

In the Mass what every sense calls bread and wine (accidents showing and composing the thing) is believed and preached as the highest God, and commanded to communicants and bystanders under latria — the cult Pontificians themselves wall off from every lesser cult.
464: That is the highest species of idolatry — which even Pontificians never deny if Transsubstantiation is not supposed, and must not deny without that hypothesis.

They cannot make their hypothesis certain by Revelation or Reason; and idolatry turns on God’s definition, not on whether a human opinion is true or false — whenever what is not the highest God is estimated, saluted, or given highest cult as if it were.
465: (3)(b) Instituted praxis from Christ binds every communicant to the cup and wine no less than to the bread.
Mass and Transsubstantiation’s rationale snatch that cup from all the laity — so it also hits the second table, withdrawing from the neighbor what Christ ordered by ‘Do this.’
466: (4) Faith and praxis of the first centuries: if the earliest Christians had professed Transsubstantiation, none then mistook ‘This is my body / blood.’
That dogma’s rumor would have flown at once to neighboring Jews and Gentiles and met not only contradiction but every hiss — from such fervent mystery-defenders it could not have stayed quiet.
467: Yet we nowhere read that even once from the fiercest enemies — Trypho, Celsus, Julian, Porphyry — who hunted every handle to calumniate Christian dogmas.
Nor from the careful apologists Justin, Tertullian, Origen, Arnobius, Minucius Felix.
468: Thyestean banquet charges stuck to Gnostics alone (maliciously counted as Christians); true Christians never even mentioned the Eucharist there, much less explained or defended this mystery — mere calumny, exploded.
And the ancients’ constant lack of later Transsubstantiation-rites (Adoration, Elevation, Circumgestation) amply shows they utterly ignored Transsubstantiation.
